props.name: type
props.doc: The policy. `single` closes the others when one opens — a set of tabs in disguise, and the right shape when the panels are alternatives. `multiple` lets the reader open what they want, which is the right shape when the panels are sections of one thing.

props.name: open
props.doc: The open ids. Controlled; omit for uncontrolled.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: The heading level for the triggers. 3 by default — see above.

props.name: title
props.doc: The question. Required — an alert dialog without one is a wall.

props.name: description
props.doc: What happens if they agree. Not decoration: this is the consequence.

props.name: destructive
props.doc: Whether confirming DESTROYS something. It changes which action is safe, and therefore which one takes focus — and it colours the confirm button. It does not change the layout, because a destructive question is not a different shape.

props.name: ratio
props.doc: Width over height: `16 / 9`, `1`, `4 / 3`.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Alias of `semantic`, kept for the call sites that already use it.

props.name: hue
props.doc: A spectrum hue instead of a semantic role. There is no glyph for a hue — a hue is not a meaning — so this path shows the label alone.

props.name: host
props.doc: Override the host surface. By default it is read from context.

props.name: asChild
props.doc: Render the child element instead of a `<button>`, keeping its styles.

props.name: variant
props.doc: The name of a decision, not a colour. `danger` is a role; `red` would be a value pretending to be a choice, and it breaks the moment the theme moves.

props.name: size
props.doc: The control height, from `CONTROL`. `md` is the default AND the accessible minimum — `CONTROL.md` and `TARGET.min` are the same number, so the default is not a compromise.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Inert: not focusable, not pressable, and it says so to a screen reader.

props.name: forcedState
props.doc: Force a state for a screenshot or a test. The interaction is CSS, so a still frame cannot show hover or press. This applies the layer's own declarations through a class — a harness for looking, not a second implementation of the state.

props.name: icon
props.doc: A glyph before the label.

props.name: iconRight
props.doc: A glyph after the label.

props.name: fullWidth
props.doc: Fill the container. For a form's primary action, not for a toolbar.

props.name: type
props.doc: Defaults to `button`, because a button inside a form that submits by accident is a bug the platform will happily commit for you.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Busy. The label stays, so the button does not change width mid-press.

props.name: iconOnly
props.doc: No visible label. Requires `ariaLabel` — an icon-only button with no name is a button a screen reader cannot describe.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: The accessible name when there is no visible one.

props.name: href
props.doc: Renders an `<a>` instead of a `<button>`. A link that navigates is a link, and a screen reader announces it differently.

props.name: rel
props.doc: Required with `target="_blank"`: without it the new tab can reach back through `window.opener`.

props.name: label
props.doc: Required: a group of controls with no name is a group a reader cannot describe.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: Stack them instead of joining them side by side.

props.name: calendar
props.doc: Which calendar to lay out. `jalali` is the Solar Hijri calendar, and it is not a formatting option: its months are 31/30/29 days, its year starts on the March equinox, and its week starts on Saturday. A Gregorian grid with Persian month names would be wrong eight days out of twelve.

props.name: lang
props.doc: The language for the month, weekday and day labels.

props.name: surface
props.doc: What this card IS in the hierarchy, not which ladder step it wants. It used to be `surfaceLevel?: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4` — a raw depth, and a raw depth cannot be checked: at level 3 the old resolver still drew a rim of 1, which the contract says belongs to chrome and work, not to a surface three steps up. `chrome` is the level the card has always sat at.

props.name: error
props.doc: The validation message. A checkbox validates: "you must accept the terms" is a real error, and it was the one thing the other five inputs had and this did not. It is a STRING, not a boolean — an error the reader cannot read is a red box.

props.name: title
props.doc: The trigger's label.

props.name: open
props.doc: Controlled open state. Omit for uncontrolled.

props.name: headingLevel
props.doc: Wrap the trigger in a heading of this level. An accordion's triggers MUST be headings — that is how a screen reader navigates between them, and it is the one part of the disclosure pattern that cannot be left to the consumer. A single disclosure is usually not a heading, which is why this is off by default and why `Accordion` turns it on.

props.name: error
props.doc: The validation message. A date can be invalid — out of range, in the past, not a working day — and the Input underneath has carried an `error` all along. The wrapper simply never passed it through, which is the same defect as the Button's swallowed handlers: a prop that stops one layer short.

props.name: dragThreshold
props.doc: How far the handle must be dragged before it counts as a dismissal.

props.name: name
props.doc: The field's name, which is also the key its validator is registered under.

props.name: hint
props.doc: A hint under the label. Announced, and replaced by the error when there is one.

props.name: required
props.doc: Mark the field required, and say so to a screen reader.

props.name: accept
props.doc: Passed to the input, so the platform can filter the picker.

props.name: active
props.doc: Whether the trap is armed. A scope that is always on is a prison.

props.name: onEscape
props.doc: Called when the reader presses Escape. A trap MUST have an exit. If this is not given, the component still lets Escape through to the document — it does not swallow it, because swallowing the only key that could free the reader is worse than not trapping.

props.name: onSubmit
props.doc: Called with the values only when every field passes. A form that submits with invalid data is a form that lost the argument with itself.

props.name: onInvalid
props.doc: Called on every submit attempt, valid or not.

props.name: validators
props.doc: Per-field validators, keyed by field name.

props.name: defaultValues
props.doc: The values the form starts with.

props.name: noValidate
props.doc: Turn the browser's own validation off — this one is better and it is ours.

props.name: level
props.doc: The DOCUMENT level, which decides the element: 1 is `<h1>`. It is not the visual size. `size` is.

props.name: size
props.doc: The VISUAL size, as a step on the engine's scale. Omitted, it follows the document level — `h1` is level 7, `h2` is 6, and so on down to level 4. Given, it overrides, because a card's heading is structurally an `h3` and visually whatever the card needs.

props.name: truncate
props.doc: Truncate to one line.

props.name: trigger
props.doc: The element the reader lingers on. Receives the ARIA wiring.

props.name: openDelay
props.doc: How long the pointer must rest before it opens.

props.name: closeDelay
props.doc: How long it waits before closing, so the pointer can travel into it.

props.name: open
props.doc: Controlled open state. Omit for uncontrolled.

props.name: size
props.doc: The control height. `md` is the default AND the accessible minimum — the engine's `CONTROL.md` and `TARGET.min` are the same number, so the default is not a compromise. It was missing: `minHeight` was hardcoded to `CONTROL.md`, so every input was 44px and there was no way to ask for a denser one.

props.name: prefix
props.doc: Rendered before the field. A unit or a protocol — not a label.

props.name: suffix
props.doc: Rendered after the field.

props.name: keys
props.doc: The key combination, when it is more than one key. Rendered as separate caps.

props.name: htmlFor
props.doc: The id of the control this names. Required — see above.

props.name: required
props.doc: Marks it as required. The marker is visual; the input carries the ARIA.

props.name: error
props.doc: Explains what is wrong. Rendered as the danger role, and announced.

props.name: role
props.doc: Which floating surface this is. The mist derives its blur, halo, shadow and fill from this role's ladder level — a toast floats higher than a menu, so it diffuses more and casts a larger shadow.

props.name: tier
props.doc: 'hero' is the single allowed emphasised mist in an app; 'quiet' is the rest.

props.name: value
props.doc: An empty string is a legitimate value: an empty field is not zero.

props.name: length
props.doc: How many digits. Also the input's maxLength.

props.name: onComplete
props.doc: Called when the last digit arrives, so a consumer does not poll.

props.name: surface
props.doc: What this panel IS in the hierarchy, not which ladder step it wants. It used to be `surfaceLevel?: number` — a raw depth. A component that names a number cannot be checked against the contract, and two components at the same depth could disagree. `work` is the level the panel has always sat at.

props.name: trigger
props.doc: The element that opens it. Receives the ARIA wiring.

props.name: placement
props.doc: Where the engine should try to put it, before collision handling.

props.name: open
props.doc: Controlled open state. Omit for uncontrolled.

props.name: modal
props.doc: Whether the content traps focus. A popover holding a form wants the trap; one holding a paragraph does not, and trapping focus for a paragraph is a trap the reader has to escape.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: An accessible name for the surface. Required when it has no heading.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: The progressbar's accessible name, when there is no visible label.

props.name: error
props.doc: The validation message for the GROUP this radio belongs to. A radio validates as a set — "choose a plan" — and the message belongs on each member so a screen reader meets it wherever the reader is. It is a STRING, not a boolean: an error the reader cannot read is a red dot.

props.name: value
props.doc: 0 means nothing chosen.

props.name: showValue
props.doc: Show "3 of 5" beside the stars.

props.name: maxHeight
props.doc: The height it scrolls within, as a STEP IN THE SCALE. It accepted a number too, and that was ambiguous: `maxHeight={6}` could mean six pixels or step six, and the component silently chose pixels. The contract's first rule is that a value becomes a token and a selection becomes a name — so this takes a NAME. A consumer who wants pixels has `style`.

props.name: label
props.doc: An accessible name. Required when it scrolls, because it becomes a stop.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: ONE signature. It used to accept either `(value: string)` or `(event)`, and tried to tell them apart with `try { onChange(value) } catch { onChange(e) }` — which cannot work: calling an event-style handler with a string does not throw, so the catch never fired and the caller silently received a string where it expected an event. Nothing used the event form, so it is gone.

props.name: caretPosition
props.doc: Which END of the field the caret sits at. `end` is the default.

props.name: error
props.doc: The validation message. A number can be out of range.

props.name: showValue
props.doc: Show the current value beside the label.

props.name: label
props.doc: What is loading. Required — "loading" alone tells the reader nothing.

props.name: labelHidden
props.doc: Hide the label visually but keep it for a screen reader.

props.name: gap
props.doc: The gap, as a STEP IN THE SCALE — not a number of pixels.

props.name: current
props.doc: Which step is current, by id. Wins over a per-step `state`.

props.name: value
props.doc: Must match the `value` of the tab it belongs to.

props.name: hue
props.doc: A spectrum hue. Tag is Badge's sibling but not its twin: Badge carries a STATUS and needs a glyph that survives colour blindness, because colour alone collapses under every form of it. Tag carries a CATEGORY, and the label itself says which one — so the hue is decoration, not information, and no glyph is needed.

props.name: host
props.doc: Override the host surface. By default it is read from context.

props.name: level
props.doc: A step on the engine's scale, 1–8.

props.name: tone
props.doc: The text role, which decides the alpha AND the floor it has to meet.

props.name: as
props.doc: The element. Independent of `level` — see above.

props.name: caps
props.doc: Small caps with the tracking the scale declares for it.

props.name: truncate
props.doc: Truncate to one line.

props.name: checked
props.doc: Whether it is on. The one name this should have had.

props.name: value
props.doc: Deprecated: An alias of `checked`. Three names for one boolean is three things a consumer has to learn and three ways to be inconsistent — the component reads all of them, and the API table is what made that visible.

props.name: on
props.doc: Deprecated: An alias of `checked`. Use `checked`.

props.name: onChange
props.doc: Reports the NEXT value, not the event. A switch is a boolean, not a DOM node, and every consumer was writing `e.target.checked` to get here.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Required when there is no visible label.

props.name: value
props.doc: A string for `single`, an array for `multiple`.

props.name: label
props.doc: Required: a group of controls with no name is a group a reader cannot describe.

props.name: error
props.doc: The validation message. A single-select group is a required choice — "pick a view" — and the fixture declared the state before the component had it. The agreement criterion is what caught that, which is what it is for.

props.name: expanded
props.doc: Controlled expansion. Omit for uncontrolled.

props.name: selected
props.doc: The selected node, or null.

props.name: as
props.doc: Render as something other than a span — a heading, a label, a div.

props.name: focusable
props.doc: Show it when it takes focus. For skip links, which must become visible.
